settings.title: Sleeves that slip inside
settings.text: Wide openings take a kimono's long sleeves — or a chunky knit — without bunching.

settings.title: A collar that leaves the emon open
settings.text: The collar follows the eased-back kimono collar instead of pressing it flat. Turn it up on cold days and it wraps your neck — no scarf needed.

settings.title: A back that makes room for the obi
settings.text: The back opens over the obi bow and falls in a soft, wide line.

settings.title: A tie, not a squeeze
settings.text: A cord from the hips ties at the front, so nothing presses on the obi. Pull it tighter for a sharper shape.

settings.name: Sumi Black
settings.text: Sumi is the black of calligraphy ink — deep and quiet.

settings.name: Usuzumi Gray
settings.text: Usuzumi is ink thinned with water: a soft, pale grey.

settings.name: Hitomi Ito
settings.text: Born into a Zen temple in Gion, Kyoto, Hitomi is a master of kimono dressing and the founder of enso, a studio that carries the Japanese sense of beauty into the present. She works with brands and artists in Japan and abroad.

settings.name: Lin Li
settings.text: With roots in both Japan and China and an education in London, Lin designs with a minimal, careful hand.

settings.name: KAPOK KNOT
settings.text: Founded in answer to mass production and waste, KAPOK KNOT makes warm clothing from kapok — a plant fibre that needs no feathers or fur.

settings.question: What size is it?
settings.answer: One size (F). The coat is cut loose so it can go over a kimono or a heavy knit, and the tie lets you adjust the shape.

settings.question: How long does delivery take?
settings.answer: Shipping is free worldwide. Orders ship from Japan within 3–5 business days; international delivery typically takes 7–14 days.

settings.question: Will I pay import duties or VAT?
settings.answer: Your order ships from Japan, and import duties and VAT are not included in our price. They are calculated and added at checkout, so you see the full total before you pay. We settle them with the courier, so there is nothing more to pay on delivery.

settings.question: How do I wash it?
settings.answer: Machine wash on a hand-wash cycle inside a laundry net, spin well, then reshape and hang to dry. Avoid fabric softener. Because the kapok is untreated, a trace of natural plant oil may show after washing — it rinses out with water.

settings.question: What if something is wrong with my order?
settings.answer: If your item arrives faulty or not as described, we'll replace or refund it at our cost. Your statutory consumer rights always apply.

settings.heading:
Born from the kimono.
Worn with anything.
settings.sub: Cut to make room for a kimono's sleeves, emon and obi — and padded with kapok, a fibre that grows on trees. Created with kimono artist Hitomi Ito and designer Lin Li.
settings.ship_note: Free worldwide shipping · Duties & VAT added at checkout
settings.story_heading: A winter coat the kimono never had.
settings.story_body:
Warm, padded coats were made for Western clothes. Over a kimono they crush the long sleeves, push down the emon — the back of the collar, eased away from the nape — and press against the obi tied at the back. So kimono wearers have long had to choose between staying warm and wearing a kimono well.

We set out to change that. In June 2023, kimono artist Hitomi Ito asked us for a coat that would make room for all three. With designer Lin Li, we spent twice our usual development time on prototypes until a padded coat could do it.
settings.kimono_body: Over a kimono, the sleeves, the emon and the obi all keep their line — so winter no longer means choosing between staying warm and dressing the way you love.
settings.design_heading: Sleeves, emon, obi. Room for all three.
settings.design_intro: Each answers a problem kimono wearers know well — and the same room makes it easy to layer anything underneath.
settings.design_note: Buttoned cuffs keep the wind out.
settings.design_quote: Over a kimono it follows the emon, so there's no pressure on the neck, and the back opens to fit the obi beautifully.
settings.everyday_body: Over jeans, a dress or a heavy knit, it reads as a sculptural wrap coat. One size, a relaxed drape — tie it loose or cinch it in.
settings.everyday_quote: I wear it with everyday clothes, not kimono. I was amazed how light it is, and it's warm even with a thick knit underneath. People always ask where it's from.
settings.material_heading: Warmth in the spirit of shōjin.
settings.material_body:
In Japan's Buddhist temples, shōjin ryōri is cooked without meat or fish, following the precept against taking life. Kapok brings that spirit to winter clothing.

It is the soft fibre from the seed pods of the kapok tree — hollow, one-eighth the weight of cotton — and harvesting it takes no feathers, no fur and no felled trees. After years of joint development with a Japanese textile maker, we turned it into a thin padding sheet: down-like warmth, without the bulk.
